thread:
maya (api-sre): seeing a sudden 5xx spike for hosted API from EU/UK users, starts ~02:01 UTC. Errors are TLS handshake failures (early). Cloudflare edge metrics show increased handshake timeouts and SNI ERRs. :frowning:

incident-bot: Paging sahil (oncall) — high-priority: api-redwood-hosted: spike in TLS handshake failures — 5xx rate 12% over 2m.

sahil (oncall): on it. grabbing quick health checks + curl from a few regions.

maya (api-sre): fwiw observability shows Datadog traces delayed ~90s in the window, so dashboards might be stale. logs show origin responded 200, but client side sees TLS alert.

leah (support): getting multiple customer tickets about 502/524s in EU. Customers mention mobile apps failing on TLS.

eli (incident-manager): declared incident: CDN/TLS/third-party. Impact: Hosted API (eu-west region) primarily. Start timeline + comms. Leah open status page draft?

leah (support): drafting status: "We are investigating increased TLS handshake errors affecting EU customers. Investigating CDN provider (Cloudflare) and routing to origins."

sahil (oncall): quick probes —
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* SSL connection using TLS1.3 / TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* TLS handshake fails: "SSL_connect: unexpected eof while reading"
```

sahil (oncall): also seeing increased SYN retries to cloudflare edge IPs from our egress. ping spikes + connection resets.

ops-bot: Note: recent Cloudflare edge changes deployed ~01:45 UTC (WAF ruleset update + edge routing policy tweak). Possible correlation.

maya (api-sre): can we rollback that WAF routing tweak to test? darren?

darren (platform): I can revert the routing policy to previous set in CF, but that requires a short DNS reload — will take ~3m to propagate across CF POPs. doing it now as a test.

sahil (oncall): while darren works that, let's enable route fallback to our direct origin (bypass CF proxy) for a subset of traffic (canary) — adding a short-lived A record to point api-eu-canary.redwood -> origin ip, TTL 30s, and add canary routing in our gateway. That will tell if the issue is CF or origin.

maya (api-sre): good call. I pushed the canary route via router set-route canary:europe -> origin-ip (tcp) and updated DNS.

sahil (oncall): results: canary traffic to origin shows normal TLS handshakes and low latencies. So origin seems fine. This points at Cloudflare/edge.

eli (incident-manager): summary for comms: "Root-cause suspected: Cloudflare edge routing/SNI handshake failures impacting EU POPs; origin healthy. We're coordinating with Cloudflare and running mitigations (route canaries, revert edge routing tweak)."

leah (support): posted interim status and set customer severity to "investigating". Customers with active incidents flagged for 1:1 updates.

incident-bot: Noted: oncall handoff in 30m scheduled (02:35 UTC). Include next oncall if still active.

sahil (oncall): opened ticket with Cloudflare support, attaching pcap and curl output (edge IPs: 190.93.x.x / 104.16.x.x range) and SNI failures. Ticket ID: CF-987654321.

Cloudflare support (via email snippet): "We see elevated handshake timeouts from a subset of EU POPs correlated with a routing flap during a config rollout. Engineers are investigating. Suggest disabling new routing policy if possible as a mitigation."

darren (platform): revert completed. CF reports the revert pushed at 02:07 UTC. I'm keeping the canary route live for a bit to gather comparative metrics.

sahil (oncall): after revert, global handshake timeouts dropped from 12% -> ~4% over 6m, but EU still shows hotspots in a few POPs (Frankfurt and London).

maya (api-sre): Datadog traces are catching up now — confirming handshake success rate improvement on canary, but some CF edge IPs still returning TLS alerts.

eli (incident-manager): escalation: if CF can't remediate quickly, contingency is to expand canary/direct routing for eu traffic and activate temporary edge-bypass pool for critical customers. We should estimate cost and performance hit.

leah (support): compiling customer list for priority escalation (SLA customers + heavy producers). sending to eli and darren.

sahil (oncall): mitigation step 2: throttle routing to problematic POPs via Cloudflare dashboard (traffic steering -> block/avoid specific POP IDs). Doing avoid for LON/FRK for now.

ops-bot: action: traffic steering set to avoid POPs LON1, FRA3 for account redwood-prod by sahil at 02:14:12 UTC.

sahil (oncall): after avoiding those POPs handshake errors fall to ~1.2% overall. Latency for EU clients increases ~60-120ms depending on fallbacks.

maya (api-sre): monitoring: no origin CPU issues. KV cache and prefix cache unaffected. Batching still fine. CPU ondedicated nodes stable.

darren (platform): prepping script to accelerate canary expansion: route 25% -> origin direct, 75% -> CF, TTL 20s, and monitor error budget. will hold off until we get final from CF.

Cloudflare support (update): "We have mitigated the routing flap. A full fix is deploying; ETA ~45 minutes for all POPs to converge. Recommend keeping avoid list until confirmed."

eli (incident-manager): set next update cadence 15m. Leah will post customer update: mitigation in place, engineering working with CDN provider, no data loss, degraded latency for some EU customers.

leah (support): update posted. #customers: initial impact window ~02:01 UTC -> ongoing. giving guidance: retry/backoff in client SDK (we'll push an advisory snippet).

sahil (oncall): note: our auth provider (third-party auth) saw an unrelated rate limit alert earlier, but not correlated to TLS failures. double-checked tokens and 401s — separate incident.

maya (api-sre): also noticed observability ingestion lag earlier — Datadog acknowledged delayed log ingestion ~02:00-02:10 UTC. caused some noise in earliest minutes.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to SEV2.

eli (incident-manager): decision log: revert CF routing tweak -> partial success; applied POP avoid list -> reduced errors; canary direct routing proves origin healthy. Next steps: keep avoid list + monitor until CF confirms full fix; prepare canary expansion plan if CF ETA slips beyond 45m.

sahil (oncall): assigning follow-ups: darren -> prepare canary expansion script + rollback; maya -> collect pcap + handshake logs for CF; leah -> customer comms cadence and one-on-ones; eli -> coordinate with Cloudflare PM.

darren (platform): will have canary script ready in 10m.

maya (api-sre): uploaded pcap and logs to CF ticket. CF engineer asked for TLS versions — we run TLS1.3 preferred, fallback TLS1.2 allowed.

Cloudflare support (final update): "Fix deployed, POPs converging. Please remove avoid rules at your discretion. We'll continue to monitor 60m. Apologies for impact."

sahil (oncall): removing avoid list now, watching metrics. handshake failure rates stable ~0.3% (baseline).

eli (incident-manager): declaring incident resolved at 02:45 UTC. moving to postmortem phase. Action items assigned.

leah (support): updating status page: resolved, root cause: Cloudflare edge routing flap during a config rollout causing intermittent TLS handshakes for EU POPs. Next steps: postmortem + improve rollback safeguards and observability gaps.

maya (api-sre): notes for postmortem: - Improve end-to-end SNI handshake synthetic tests from multiple POPs - Add CF routing policy rollout guardrails in infra CI - Add quicker direct-origin canary tooling - Datadog ingestion alert tuning to avoid delayed visibility.

eli (incident-manager): thanks team. we'll schedule a 30m postmortem within the next 48h. :white_check_mark:
